parsed.title: Deep Learning and Attention for Computer Vision: From Foundations to Research
parsed.abstract: This textbook prepares students to read, reproduce, and extend contemporary research in deep learning for computer vision with a structured progression from classical pattern recognition to attention-based models. It begins with statistical learning principles and optimization that underpin modern neural networks, then develops core deep learning methods for images through convolutional architectures. The text introduces attention mechanisms and transformers, explaining their mathematical foundations, design choices, and applications to vision. Throughout, it integrates implementation insights, common pitfalls, and comparative perspectives between CNNs and attention-based models. The final component emphasizes research workflow, including experimental design, evaluation, and reproducibility, enabling students to critically assess and build upon current literature.

chapters.chapter_title: Foundations of Statistical Learning for Vision
chapters.chapter_description: Covers probabilistic modeling, loss functions, generalization, and optimization, linking linear models and feature representations to the need for deep architectures.

chapters.chapter_title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Image Understanding
chapters.chapter_description: Introduces convolution, pooling, backpropagation, and training pipelines, surveying canonical and modern CNN architectures (e.g., residual networks) and transfer learning.
Explains self-attention, multi-head attention, and encoder-decoder designs, then applies them to vision (ViT and hybrids), highlighting inductive biases and computational trade-offs.

chapters.chapter_title: Research Methods: Datasets, Evaluation, and Reproducibility
chapters.chapter_description: Details experimental design, benchmarks and metrics, ablations, robustness and interpretability, and best practices for reading, reproducing, and extending research papers.
